comparisons.peer_topic: Gross margin financial results and VMware impact
comparisons.peer_summary: Gross margin increased to $32,509 million in fiscal year 2024 from $24,690 million in fiscal year 2023, primarily due to VMware contributions offset by higher amortization of acquisition-related intangible assets. As a percentage of net revenue, gross margin decreased to 63% from 69%, driven by the same amortization factors, less favorable semiconductor product mix, and offsets from infrastructure software margins.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclose specific factors driving consolidated gross margin performance in 2024, though the outcomes and drivers differ significantly. Intel reports a decrease in gross margin driven by large non-cash impairment and accelerated depreciation charges ($3.3 billion) related to manufacturing asset capacity and inventory charges ($922 million). In contrast, Broadcom reports an increase in gross margin dollars ($32,509 million) but a decrease in margin percentage (63% vs 69%) driven primarily by higher amortization of acquisition-related intangible assets from the VMware Merger and less favorable semiconductor product mix. Both cite specific charge types (intel: impairment/depreciation; broadcom: amortization) impacting their respective margin metrics.

sentences.text: Our consolidated gross margin in 2024 decreased by $4.4 billion, or 20%, compared to 2023 due primarily to higher 2024 impairment charges and accelerated depreciation.

Upon completing an asset re-use assessment, we impaired certain construction-in-progress assets and accelerated depreciation for certain in-use manufacturing assets that resulted in $3.3 billion of charges in 2024.

Our 2024 gross margin also decreased due to lower revenue, higher unit cost primarily from an increased mix of Intel 4 and Intel 7 products, higher period charges due to $922 million in Gaudi AI accelerator inventory-related charges recognized in 2024, and higher factory start-up costs.
Gross margin was $32,509 million for fiscal year 2024 compared to $24,690 million for fiscal year 2023.
The increase was primarily due to contributions from VMware, partially offset by higher amortization of acquisition-related intangible assets from the VMware Merger.
As a percentage of net revenue, gross margin was 63% and 69% of net revenue for the fiscal years 2024 and 2023, respectively.
The decrease was primarily due to higher amortization of acquisition-related intangible assets from the VMware Merger.
In addition, gross margin contributions from our infrastructure software segment were partially offset by less favorable margin within the semiconductor solutions segment driven by product mix.

comparisons.peer_summary: Consolidated gross margin improved to 22% in 2024 from -9% in 2023, aided by increased average selling prices and manufacturing cost reductions, despite the prior year's inventory write-downs and lower costs from selling previously written-down inventory in 2024.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies discuss inventory-related impacts on gross margin in 2024. Intel cites $922 million in Gaudi AI accelerator inventory-related charges as a driver of decreased gross margin. Micron discloses that while gross margin improved to 22% in 2024 from -9% in 2023, the improvement was aided by lower costs in 2024 from the sale of inventories written down in 2023, indicating a direct link between prior-year write-downs and 2024 cost of sales. Both identify inventory valuation issues (charges/write-downs) as a specific operational factor affecting gross margin metrics.

sentences.text: Our 2024 gross margin also decreased due to lower revenue, higher unit cost primarily from an increased mix of Intel 4 and Intel 7 products, higher period charges due to $922 million in Gaudi AI accelerator inventory-related charges recognized in 2024, and higher factory start-up costs.

Our consolidated gross margin percentage improved to 22% for 2024 from negative 9% for 2023, as a result of improvements in margins for both DRAM and NAND products, primarily due to increases in average selling prices, and manufacturing cost reductions, the effects of charges to write down inventories to their NRV in 2023 and lower costs in 2024 from the sale of inventories written down in 2023 (as detailed in "Inventory NRV write-downs" below).
